title: DailyMed — VANCOMYCIN HYDROCHLORIDE injection, powder, lyophilized, for solution (Gland Pharma Limited)

claims.text: Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibacterial indicated in adults and pediatric patients (neonates and older).
claims.byte_quote: Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection is a glycopeptide antibacterial indicated in adult and pediatric patients (neonates and older)

claims.text: Vancomycin is a tricyclic glycopeptide whose bactericidal action comes primarily from inhibiting cell-wall biosynthesis.
claims.byte_quote: The bactericidal action of vancomycin results primarily from inhibition of cell-wall biosynthesis

claims.text: Vancomycin is indicated for septicemia (bloodstream infection) due to susceptible MRSA and coagulase negative staphylococci.
claims.byte_quote:
for the treatment of septicemia due to: 
 Susceptible isolates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and coagulase negative staphylococci.

claims.text: In penicillin-allergic patients (or those who cannot take / have failed penicillins or cephalosporins), vancomycin covers methicillin-susceptible staphylococci for septicemia.
claims.byte_quote: Methicillin-susceptible staphylococci in penicillin-allergic patients, or those patients who cannot receive or who have failed to respond to other drugs, including penicillins or cephalosporins.

claims.text: Vancomycin treats infective endocarditis due to MRSA; viridans group streptococci, Streptococcus gallolyticus (formerly S. bovis), Enterococcus species, and Corynebacterium species.
claims.byte_quote: Viridans group streptococci Streptococcus gallolyticus (previously known as Streptococcus bovis ), Enterococcus species and Corynebacterium species.

claims.text: For enterococcal endocarditis, vancomycin must be combined with an aminoglycoside.
claims.byte_quote: For enterococcal endocarditis, use Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection in combination with an aminoglycoside.

claims.text: Vancomycin treats early-onset prosthetic valve endocarditis caused by Staphylococcus epidermidis, combined with rifampin and an aminoglycoside.
claims.byte_quote: for the treatment of early-onset prosthetic valve endocarditis caused by Staphylococcus epidermidis in combination with rifampin and an aminoglycoside.

claims.text: Vancomycin treats skin and skin structure infections due to susceptible MRSA and coagulase negative staphylococci.
claims.byte_quote:
for the treatment of skin and skin structure infections due to: 
 Susceptible isolates of MRSA and coagulase negative staphylococci.

claims.text: Vancomycin treats lower respiratory tract infections due to susceptible MRSA.
claims.byte_quote:
for the treatment of lower respiratory tract infections due to: 
 Susceptible isolates of MRSA

claims.text: Adult dose with normal renal function is 2 g/day, given as 500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours.
claims.byte_quote: The usual daily intravenous dose is 2 grams divided either as 500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours.

claims.text: Pediatric dose (aged 1 month and older) is 10 mg/kg per dose every 6 hours, each over at least 60 minutes.
claims.byte_quote: The usual intravenous dosage of vancomycin is 10 mg/kg per dose given every 6 hours. Each dose should be administered over a period of at least 60 minutes.

claims.text: Neonatal dose: initial 15 mg/kg, then 10 mg/kg every 12 hours in the first week of life and every 8 hours thereafter up to 1 month of age.
claims.byte_quote: In neonates, an initial dose of 15 mg/kg is suggested, followed by 10 mg/kg every 12 hours for neonates in the 1 st week of life and every 8 hours thereafter up to the age of 1 month.

claims.text: In premature infants vancomycin clearance falls as postconceptional age decreases, so longer dosing intervals may be needed.
claims.byte_quote: In premature infants, vancomycin clearance decreases as postconceptional age decreases. Therefore, longer dosing intervals may be necessary in premature infants.

claims.text: In renal impairment the initial dose should be no less than 15 mg/kg; functionally anephric patients get 15 mg/kg initially then 1.9 mg/kg/24 hr.
claims.byte_quote: For functionally anephric patients, an initial dose of 15 mg/kg of body weight should be given to achieve prompt therapeutic serum concentration. A dose of 1.9 mg/kg/24 hr should be given after the initial dose of 15 mg/kg.

claims.text: Each IV dose should be administered over a period of 60 minutes or greater to reduce infusion reactions.
claims.byte_quote: administer Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection in a diluted solution over 60 minutes or greater

claims.text: Vancomycin is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to vancomycin.
claims.byte_quote: Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to vancomycin.

claims.text: Vancomycin can cause acute kidney injury including acute renal failure, mainly from interstitial nephritis or less commonly acute tubular necrosis.
claims.byte_quote: Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection can result in acute kidney injury (AKI), including acute renal failure, mainly due to interstitial nephritis or less commonly acute tubular necrosis.

claims.text: AKI risk rises with higher vancomycin serum levels, prolonged exposure, concomitant nephrotoxic drugs, concomitant piperacillin-tazobactam, volume depletion, pre-existing renal impairment, and critical illness.
claims.byte_quote: The risk of AKI increases with higher vancomycin serum levels, prolonged exposure, concomitant administration of other nephrotoxic drugs, concomitant administration of piperacillin-tazobactam

claims.text: Concomitant piperacillin/tazobactam plus vancomycin increases acute kidney injury incidence versus vancomycin alone.
claims.byte_quote: Increased incidence of acute kidney injury in patients receiving concomitant piperacillin/tazobactam and vancomycin as compared to vancomycin alone.

claims.text: Concomitant vancomycin and anesthetic agents has been associated with erythema and histamine-like flushing.
claims.byte_quote: Concomitant administration of vancomycin and anesthetic agents has been associated with erythema and histaminelike flushing.

claims.text: Ototoxicity risk is higher in older patients, those on higher doses, with underlying hearing loss, on concomitant ototoxic agents (e.g. aminoglycoside), or with renal impairment.
claims.byte_quote: The risk is higher in older patients, patients who are receiving higher doses, who have an underlying hearing loss, who are receiving concomitant therapy with another ototoxic agent, such as an aminoglycoside or who have underlying renal impairment.

claims.text: Reversible neutropenia has been reported; patients on prolonged therapy or concomitant neutropenia-causing drugs should have periodic leukocyte counts.
claims.byte_quote: Reversible neutropenia has been reported in patients receiving Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection

claims.text: No available data on vancomycin use in pregnant women inform a drug-associated risk of major birth defects or miscarriage (pregnancy section).
claims.byte_quote: “vancomycin infusion reaction”, which manifests as pruritus and erythema that involves the face, neck and upper torso

cites: Byrd RA, Gries CL, Buening M. Developmental Toxicology Studies of Vancomycin Hydrochloride Administered Intravenously to Rats and Rabbits. Fundam Appl Toxicol 1994; 23: 590-597.
